quotes.text: Learn how to collect and report taxes for recurring payments.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: To calculate tax for recurring payments, Stripe offers Stripe Tax and tax rates:
This is a Stripe Tax for when tax-calculation is stripe-tax.
This is a Tax Rates for when tax-calculation is tax-rates.
If your customer has a default payment method, the first invoice of the subscription is paid automatically.

findings: The November same-URL capture is only a 14-line index naming the Stripe Tax and Tax Rates query variants (new 5-14). It contains no tax calculation, subscription, invoice, payment, or refund instructions. The collection diff deletes the old guide body and adds only the index and two variant links (diff 3-13, 570-571). This is a rendering/navigation change, not evidence that either tax route was deprecated.

The May same-URL capture includes both variant bodies explicitly (old 8-18, 413-417): Stripe Tax for Customer v1 and manual Tax Rates. The current 107-line [[source-stripe-billing-taxes-collect]] is based on that May raw (source 4-7, 105-107), and its core flows are dated historical evidence, not November-verified behavior.

Old Stripe Tax details include server preview invoice with IP only as an initial estimate, customer address collection through client Elements without an Intent, server Customer location validation, and subscription creation (old 28-34, 104-148, 188-278). The November index does not confirm or contradict those mechanics.

Old Tax Rates details include subscription/item rates with item override and up to five rates per item, draft renewal-invoice changes, and fixed or dynamic Checkout rates (old 419-425, 463-469, 471-559). The November index does not confirm or contradict those mechanics.

Existing source 70 shows payment_behavior default_incomplete in a consolidated example, but old 257-271 omits it from the example and old 278 conditions it on wanting to confirm newly collected payment details instead of allowing a saved default payment method to pay the first invoice automatically. Preserve that payment-state qualification in any later source correction; the new index supplies no replacement behavior.
historical_claims_to_preserve: The May 2026 full guide remains the pinned factual evidence for Stripe Tax versus manual Tax Rates, costs and third-party integrations (old 8-18); a November navigation index does not revoke its dated claims.

The May guide's client/server and Customer v1 scope must remain dated: preview invoice and customer/subscription writes are server steps, Elements collection and confirmation are client steps, and the captured path is labeled Customer v1 (old 20-23, 28, 104, 146, 188-192, 246-250).

The May payment boundary is conditional: an existing default payment method can pay the first invoice automatically; use default_incomplete when intending to confirm newly collected details, and protect the invoice confirmation client secret (old 274-278).
The May Tax Rates branch's approximately one-hour renewal draft window and Checkout fixed/dynamic exclusion are dated facts (old 463-469, 559). No November variant body was captured here.
conflicts: Current source 70 unconditionally includes payment_behavior default_incomplete while the old source example omits it (old 257-271) and explains it as conditional (old 278). This is a pre-existing summary qualification issue, not a November change; a later correction should state the condition without inferring payment success from the example.
No direct contradiction between the new index and the old Stripe Tax/Tax Rates variant instructions is established. The new route merely omits their bodies (new 9-14; old 14-569).
unresolved_questions: The two variant URLs linked on new 13-14 were not captured or read for this exact job; their current instructions, UI/account variant scope, and availability cannot be verified from this index.
The new index does not establish account-specific Stripe Tax registration, payment/tax collection outcomes, or that old May API examples remain current.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/taxes/collect-taxes, the November 7 capture establishes only a tax-for-recurring-payments index and links to Stripe Tax and Tax Rates variants (new 5-14). The May full capture supplied both variant bodies, including the Stripe Tax preview/address/Customer v1 and subscription steps (old 14-28, 104-148, 188-278) and the Tax Rates subscription/Checkout branch (old 413-559). [[source-stripe-billing-taxes-collect]] summarizes that May evidence at source 11-96. This new index does not establish present variant behavior or any tax or payment outcome.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/billing/taxes/collect-taxes, the observed change is navigation-only: new 11-14 routes to two query variants where old 16-18 and 413-417 began their full bodies. It is not a deprecation of either approach and does not justify replacing the dated mechanics in [[source-stripe-billing-taxes-collect]]. Preserve May Customer v1/client-server labels, IP-estimate uncertainty (old 20-34, 104-106), and conditional first-invoice payment behavior (old 274-278); source 70 currently compresses that condition. The variant targets were not read for this job, so current API behavior, eligibility and collection success remain unverified.
